what: The independent certification of the refutation of Erdős Problem #488 (formal-conjectures PR #5297): the pre-registered questions P1–P7, each read back from the run.
undecided: The discovery is Declan Gessel's, made with OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra in Codex (2026-09-05). This record decides whether his Lean proof refutes the entry as it stands in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, on the kernels run here, with the arithmetic re-derived independently. It does not decide who found the counterexample first (a reading), the least counterexample, or anything the four checkers not run here would add.

facts.statement: φ(Q) = ∏(p − 1) over the odd primes below 257 (φ computed from the factorisation)

python.statement: |O| = 53, where O = the odd primes below 257 (own sieve, cross-checked by naive trial division)
totient(Q) = phi, Q = prod of O, phi = prod (p-1) over O; totient from trial-division factorisation and the general formula prod p^(e-1)(p-1)

P4.correction: the JavaScript decider's first control (3·Q < 15·φ) was itself true, since φ/Q > 1/5; corrected to 14 before recording; the Python decider's author computed 14 independently

P5.reading: no counterexample in the family of smooth bands (T, cT] with exact counts to 10^7; ratios approach 2 only for one to four generators, where an elementary bound keeps them below 2

P7.how: the build fails: decide proves the planted inequality false

deviations.text: The pre-registration gives DeepMind's Mathlib as b7eb3304; that is the plausible package's pin. Mathlib is v4.33.1 at 0df444a3 (the entry's lake-manifest.json; fc-cache.log).

The pre-registered rule names three Lean checkers (leanchecker, leanchecker-paranoid, --fresh); leanchecker-paranoid is not in Lean 4.33.1, so P3 rests on leanchecker and --fresh, with nanoda as an independent kernel. The separate re-elaboration of each source with -Ddebug.skipKernelTC=false was not run; the audit records the kernel check on by default.
The pre-registered false variant (4095 for 4096) is in fact true, 2^4095·32769^53 < 3^4095, so it would not have been a fake; the run used 1000, which is false.
